transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you, too. Um, I came in today because I'm just having a really hard time turning my thoughts off. 

Once a worry starts—like about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work—I just... I can’t seem to shelve it in my mind. It just stays there. No matter how many lists I make or how hard I try to redirect myself to something else, I just can't seem to let it go.
When you are stuck in these cycles of worry, do you notice any physical sensations, such as muscle tension, feeling restless, or feeling easily fatigued?

Yeah, definitely the muscle tension. Um, by the end of the day, my neck and shoulders just feel completely locked up. I guess I'm just bracing myself all the time without realizing it. And I actually catch myself clenching my jaw a lot, too—like when I'm answering emails, or just... sitting there listening for my mother in the next room.
Do you ever experience sudden, intense surges of overwhelming fear or discomfort that peak within a few minutes?

No, I don't think so. It's not really a sudden, intense feeling like that. It's more of a constant, steady hum of worry that's just always there in the background. I don't get those overwhelming waves of fear out of nowhere.
Over what period of time have you been experiencing these persistent worries and physical symptoms on most days?
Well, it's been going on for about a year and two months now. That's when my mother moved in with me after she had a bad fall, and it just seems like everything has been building up since then.
How much difficulty do you have in stopping or controlling these worries once they start?

It's really difficult, honestly. That's actually why I decided to come in. Once a worry starts—like if I'm thinking about my mother trying to get up in the middle of the night, or a grant report, or wondering if I missed something at work—I just can't seem to shelve it in my mind. I try to make lists, or force myself to focus on something else, but no matter how hard I try to redirect myself, I just can't stop the thoughts once they get going.
Has this persistent worry made it difficult for you to fall asleep, stay asleep, or feel rested when you wake up?

Yes, it really has. Most nights, I just lie there replaying the day in my head, you know, trying to plan for every possible problem that could happen. And then... well, if I do manage to sleep and then wake up because I hear my mother moving around, I'm usually up for an hour or two afterward just thinking. By the time I get to the library in the morning, I feel like I never really rested at all.
